drhp.business: Eureka Forbes Limited, with a legacy spanning over four decades, sells health and hygiene products and services to Indian households and institutions through its flagship Aquaguard brand and allied portfolio. Its offering spans water purifiers, vacuum cleaners (including robotic vacuum cleaners), air purifiers, water softeners and services including aftermarket filters and annual maintenance contracts. The Company was an early adopter of the direct-to-consumer model in India and reaches customers through an integrated multi-channel approach of direct sales, retail (modern and general trade) …

risks.note: The Company's growth thesis rests on converting very low category penetration into share gains. Mitigations cited include offerings at price points from entry level to premium across products and service, launch of 2X filter life products across the electric water purifier portfolio, significant investment in R&D and marketing capability, an omni-channel go-to-market with access to consumer homes, and targeted action on grey-market operations and consumer education. Financial implication flagged as negative.
risks.risk: Market risk — inability to drive category growth and market share

risks.note: Because the moat is the installed base and after-sales service network, a service failure directly threatens reputation and recurring revenue. Mitigations include fortifying the service network through infrastructure upgrades and expansion, digital capability that gives control to customers, organisational interventions such as 'Customer Day' and deep business-partner engagement, and a revamped incentive model to improve on-slot performance.
risks.risk: Consumer and reputation risk — poor customer experience damaging brand

risks.note: Unexpected supply-chain disruption can constrain product availability. Mitigations include a detailed vendor development roadmap to de-risk the supply network, progressively enhanced strategic partnerships, in-house and domestic manufacturing partnerships in key categories, and strategic up-stocking of inventory given the current geopolitical environment.
risks.risk: Supply chain risk — disruption from geopolitical or other external factors

risks.note: Exposure spans cyberattacks, ransomware, data breaches, inadequate disaster recovery and non-compliance with evolving data privacy law such as the DPDP Rules — material for a D2C business holding large volumes of consumer data. Mitigations include a detailed disaster recovery process, data security measures (customer data controls, single sign-on/multi-factor authentication, call masking), organisation-wide cybersecurity awareness training, cyber-security tooling and a DPDP implementation programme.

The transformation agenda depends on leadership depth and execution capability. Mitigations include dedicated teams and capability building for transformation initiatives, large-scale workforce training and up-skilling, employee engagement through continuous leadership connect platforms, a high-performance culture reinforced through rewards and ESOP participation, and a human rights, ethics and inclusion framework.
risks.risk: People risk — people and cultural factors hindering the transformation

risks.note: Quality and relevance drive both first purchase and the service annuity. Mitigations include design improvements such as new flow restrictors and flushing mechanisms with regular review of performance metrics, monitoring for validation of VAVE initiatives and new product development to avoid marketplace quality issues, and a structured approach to identifying, managing and reducing environmental impacts across operations.
risks.risk: Product risk — inability to enhance product quality and meet evolving customer needs

risks.note: The MD&A notes inflationary pressures strengthened toward the end of FY26 as higher crude oil prices and currency depreciation increased input and consumer costs, with inflation expected to rise before moderating — a direct margin and pricing risk for a consumer durables manufacturer.
risks.risk: Input cost inflation and currency depreciation
